rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty and measure how the closest pairs respond to slope. The scouting run has substantial resolution margin and all compounds elute well within the gradient.
Keep the fast gradient and test whether higher temperature separates the critical cluster through selectivity changes. This isolates the temperature effect while preserving a short elution time.

Test the low-temperature endpoint at the same slope to map the alternative selectivity regime. Lower temperature may separate the central cluster without requiring the substantially longer gradient used in injection 1.

Use an intermediate temperature to avoid the close-pair collisions seen at 40 and 60 C, with a slightly shallower gradient to improve separation. The last peak should still elute near eight minutes, keeping the time penalty small or zero.

Raise temperature by one grid step to open the remaining close central pair while retaining the gentler slope of injection 5. This may achieve full resolution with the last peak still below eight minutes.

Injection 6 has reached the maximum possible CRF and remains the benchmark. Test a slightly shallower gradient to assess whether full resolution can be maintained with a larger separation margin and no time penalty.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test a modestly higher starting organic fraction for a faster alternative. This changes the gradient window and may improve the limiting pair, while the first peak should remain retained.

Reduce the gradient slope to improve the limiting pair from injection 8 while preserving its higher starting organic fraction. The last peak is expected near eight minutes, potentially providing another maximum-score method with better resolution margin.

Slightly steepen injection 9’s effective slope while trimming the unused high-organic portion of the gradient. This should shorten elution modestly while keeping both critical pairs near or above baseline resolution; the maximum-score method from injection 6 remains secured.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction opens the remaining close pair in the high-temperature regime, with a shallower slope to support separation. Monitor the first two peaks for excessive compression; the maximum-score methods remain secured.

Interpolate the gradient slope between injections 8 and 9 to locate the faster edge of the full-resolution region at this starting composition. The maximum CRF is already secured; this run tests whether it can be retained with a shorter elution time than injection 9.
